name: Same Key, Every Byte
description:
A classroom application encrypts reports with a repeating 8-byte XOR key.
You intercepted one report and know its standard opening text.

Download `report.enc.txt`, recover the plaintext, and submit the flag inside it.
The attachment gives the encryption rule and the exact known prefix.
Python 3 or any equivalent local tool is allowed; no brute force is necessary.

Submit exactly one flag in `SCSS{...}` format. Flags are case-sensitive.

name: The Cube That Never Wrapped
description:
A developer encrypted a short flag using textbook RSA without padding.
Download `public-key.json`, containing the public modulus `n`, exponent `e`, and ciphertext `c`.

The flag was converted from UTF-8 bytes into a big-endian integer `m`, then `c = m^e mod n` with `e = 3`. The developer chose a message so short that `m^3 < n`. Use that fact to recover the message. You do not need to factor `n` or recover the private key. Convert the recovered integer back to big-endian bytes and decode as UTF-8. Use exact integer arithmetic; ordinary floating-point cube roots can round.

Submit exactly one flag in `SCSS{...}` format. Flags are case-sensitive.
